summary: @servicetitan/microfront-tests preinstall downloads Bun and executes a heavily obfuscated shipped payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that probes for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads the Bun runtime from oven-sh's GitHub releases (v1.3.13), unpacks it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` (`execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})`). `math_init.js` is a 727KB `@bun @bun-cjs` blob further obfuscated with a shuffled string-array rotator (`WV8StW`), a ~2000-entry mixed literal table (`n7gIxM`), and a base64-alphabet-like decoder key (`hc1jfK9`), so no destinations, commands, or file paths appear as plain literals. `setup.mjs` itself is `_0xNNNN`-obfuscated. The advertised functionality is a trivial ts-mockito re-export library, which has no relation to fetching an alternate language runtime at install time to execute an opaque 727KB payload. The package name suggests affiliation with the ServiceTitan organization; combined with the alternate-runtime install-time execution vector and obfuscation, this matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to bypass Node-only static scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
